title: Dental Innovations Group Advances AI in Dentistry
html:
Dentistry has never had more information available to guide patient care. Artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance diagnostic capabilities, salivary testing can provide new insights into disease risk, and digital technologies continue to expand what clinicians can identify and recommend.

But as innovation accelerates, dental hygienist and founder Lindsey Bieligk, RDH, MSDH, believes another challenge is becoming increasingly important:

How do we make care easier to implement in everyday dental practice?

After nearly two decades in dental hygiene and now coaching more than 40 clinicians across multiple practices, Bieligk has seen the challenge from both sides. New technologies can provide clinicians with extraordinary amounts of information, but translating that information into patient education, clinical action, follow-up, and measurable outcomes can require significant time and expertise.

That observation became the foundation for Dental Innovations Group, a healthcare technology company focused on building what Bieligk calls the “implementation layer” of dentistry.

“We’re becoming incredibly good at collecting information and identifying disease,” Bieligk said. “But the value of innovation isn’t realized simply because we have better data. It is realized when a clinician can efficiently translate that information into care and a patient can understand what to do next.”

Dental Innovations Group is developing AI-enabled platforms designed to support that transition from clinical information to action. Its initial technologies explore different areas of care, including salivary diagnostics, home-care recommendations, and myofunctional therapy, while sharing the same underlying objective: reducing the work required to consistently implement recommended care and follow up with patients.

The approach is intentionally clinician-centered.

Rather than asking dental teams to add another complex workflow, Bieligk sees an opportunity for AI to perform more of the work surrounding the clinical encounter, including organizing information, supporting education, reinforcing recommendations, facilitating follow-up, and identifying where additional clinician attention may be needed.

“The future of AI in dentistry shouldn’t be about removing clinicians from care,” Bieligk said. “It should be about removing enough of the administrative burden that clinicians can be more present in it.”

That distinction may become increasingly important as dentistry adopts more advanced diagnostics and personalized approaches to prevention. Technologies can provide deeper insights, but widespread adoption ultimately depends on whether those insights can be incorporated into the realities of a busy dental practice.

For Bieligk, that is where the next phase of dental innovation begins.

“We don’t necessarily need more information,” she said. “We need better ways to turn the information we already have into action. If AI can help us do that consistently, advanced care becomes more accessible, not only in practices with extensive time and resources, but across dentistry.”

Dental Innovations Group’s initial platforms are currently in beta development as the company works with clinicians and industry partners to refine workflows and validate real-world applications.

About Dental Innovations Group

Dental Innovations Group is a healthcare technology company developing AI-enabled solutions designed to bridge the gap between clinical information and implementation. Founded by dental hygienist Lindsey Bieligk, RDH, MSDH, the company focuses on reducing workflow burden while supporting patient understanding, engagement, adherence, and measurable outcomes.
